notice: Synthetic demonstration fixtures. No real product, line, batch or inspection data. The pinned detector outputs are fixtures, not model performance: they exist so the demo and the tests produce the same result on every machine and on a conference network with no connectivity.

scenarios.name: Clean unit
scenarios.narrative: Nothing is wrong. The platform still records evidence, because a transaction with no finding is exactly the one nobody can reconstruct later.

scenarios.name: Cosmetic finding
scenarios.narrative: A real defect that deliberately does not require approval. Approval on low-impact actions trains approvers to click through the ones that matter.

scenarios.name: Low-confidence signal
scenarios.narrative: The detector did not clear its own threshold. The platform re-inspects rather than raising a work order on a signal the model does not stand behind.

scenarios.name: Safety-relevant major defect
scenarios.narrative: The hero path. Evidence, a deterministic verdict, a held approval, and a write that only happens after a named human agrees to this exact proposal.

scenarios.name: Repeated major defect in batch
scenarios.narrative: The same defect recurring in one batch is a process fault, not a unit fault. Policy escalates from a work order to a line stop without anyone rewriting a prompt.

scenarios.name: Critical structural defect
scenarios.narrative: The highest-consequence path: line stop, quarantine, dual control. Two distinct principals must approve before anything is written.

scenarios.name: Restricted-classification frame
scenarios.narrative: A cosmetic finding that would normally auto-log. Guard G002 fires on the classification alone and forces a human to look at it.

scenarios.name: Unsafe replenishment candidate
scenarios.narrative: Synthetic fixture: a generated recommendation encounters a discontinued SKU. Deterministic policy rejects it; the model does not get a vote on the constraint.

scenarios.name: Governed warehouse replenishment
scenarios.narrative: Synthetic fixture: governed inventory evidence supports a safe candidate. Policy requires a separate inventory-manager approval before the scoped writer dry-runs the exact D365 order.
